events.speaker: user
events.text: Hi, uh, is this Martin Feld?

events.speaker: prospect
events.text: Yeah. Speaking.

events.speaker: user
events.text: Martin, it's Daniel Brooks from The Herakles. Quick heads-up, I've got an AI assistant analysing the call, it just helps me keep notes. Is that alright with you?

events.speaker: prospect
events.text: Sure. Whatever.

events.speaker: user
events.text: Thanks. So, we're a digital studio, we redesign websites, mostly for professional services firms. I was looking at the Feld and Ashcombe site this morning and, well, I've got a question more than a pitch, if that's okay.

events.speaker: prospect
events.text: Look, um, can you just... pop something over by email? I'll have a look when I get a minute.

events.speaker: user
events.text: I can do that, sure. Before I do, so I don't send you something generic, how do new clients usually find you these days?

events.speaker: prospect
events.text: Uh... referrals, mostly. Some find us online, I suppose. I don't really, I don't really know the split, to be honest.

events.speaker: user
events.text: Mm-hmm.

events.speaker: prospect
events.text: And, well, we've already got a guy who does the website. Freelancer. He's been with us, what, six years now?

events.speaker: user
events.text: Six years, that's a good run. Is he more on the maintenance side, or does he also, um, think about how the site actually brings in work?

events.speaker: prospect
events.text: Maintenance, mostly. He updates the team page. Changes the tax deadlines. That sort of thing.

events.speaker: user
events.text: Right. So one thing I noticed... on a phone, your contact form sits about four scrolls down, and there's no way to book a call. For an accounting firm in January, that's, uh, that's exactly where people drop off.

events.speaker: prospect
events.text: Huh. Four scrolls? I didn't... I never really check it on my phone.

events.speaker: user
events.text: Most directors don't. What we usually do is keep your freelancer in the loop, he still runs the updates, and we rework the structure. Clear services, online booking, client portal link right up front.

events.speaker: prospect
events.text: Okay, that's... actually, our receptionist spends half her morning on the phone just scheduling appointments.

events.speaker: user
events.text: Right.

events.speaker: prospect
events.text: Would that, I mean, would the booking tie into our calendar? We use, uh, a shared one. It's a bit of a mess.

events.speaker: user
events.text: It can, yeah. One firm we worked with, similar size to yours, cut their booking calls by about a third in the first quarter.

events.speaker: prospect
events.text: A third. Hm.

events.speaker: user
events.text: So how about this. Thirty minutes, I walk you through the mobile issues on your own site and a rough plan. Would next Tuesday or Wednesday work?

events.speaker: prospect
events.text: Oh, I mean, it's January, we're right in the thick of tax season. I can barely breathe till the end of the month. I'd like to, but...

events.speaker: user
events.text: Totally fair. When does it ease off for you?

events.speaker: prospect
events.text: Uh, first week of February? Maybe. Probably. Let me, let me think... yes. Early February.

events.speaker: user
events.text: How about I call you back Monday the third, mid-morning, and we pick a slot then? And I'll send a short email today with the screenshots.

events.speaker: prospect
events.text: Yeah. Yeah, do that. Actually, send those screenshots, I want to show my partner, Ruth. She's been going on about the website for ages!

events.speaker: user
events.text: Will do. Monday the third, around ten?

events.speaker: prospect
events.text: Ten's good. Honestly, glad you rang. Speak then.

events.speaker: user
events.text: Thanks, Martin. Talk soon.
